subject: Velox production: chunked-transfer serialization causing elevated 5xx and p95 spikes
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena@velox.ai>

Cc: support@velox.ai
Date: 2027-06-14T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Production timeouts + partial chunks from Redwood streaming (Velox account)

Jonas / Marissa —

We started seeing elevated errors this morning across our inference-enabled product (region: us-west-2). Symptoms: intermittent streaming responses that never finish (client shows socket open but no final chunk), and a big jump in 5xx errors from ~0.03% baseline to ~7.2% across the 08:00–09:00 window. P95 latency for non-streaming calls also rose ~2.4x.

Replicable on a handful of pinned requests that were stable yesterday. We captured a client trace and a short server timeline; attaching the trace and a chunked request id. Relevant IDs: request-velox-6a2, conn-1149.

This is customer-facing for us — our ops lead is escalating to our CTO. Please advise immediate mitigation steps and whether a rollback/fallback is advised. We need an ETA for a short mitigation and an RCA timeline.

Attachments: velox-client-trace-06014.json, request-samples.txt

Thanks —
Elena Martinez

Hi Elena — thanks for the quick heads-up and the traces. Sorry you're running into this. We're triaging now and I wanted to summarize immediate asks so we can move fast: 

1) Can you paste one of the exact request IDs (the full UUID) and the exact timestamp you saw the client socket still open?
2) Confirm whether you were using our streaming (chunked) endpoint or the pull/long-polling variant.

Quick next steps from our side: Marissa is investigating a potential backlog in the chunk serialization queue that can cause connections to hold open while the worker waits on a lock. If we confirm that, short term we can:  
- enable a temporary routing policy to force Velox traffic to our non-streaming endpoint (no chunking) for the next 2 hours, OR
- apply a rolling config change to reduce the per-connection batch window to 25ms which should drop queue buildup at some cost to throughput.

Both are quick mitigations; I want to coordinate before we flip anything. I'm looping in Sergio and Marissa from the infra/runtime team for triage. I'll schedule a 30-min emergency sync in 20 minutes.

Jonas

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production timeouts + partial chunks from Redwood streaming (Velox account)

Quick initial findings from the first set of logs (attached):

- Observed elevated "chunk_serialize_ms" per-worker (median 2ms -> 18ms, tail up to 340ms) during the window.
- The worker thread that serializes/flushes chunked responses is frequently blocked waiting on a short-lived lock held by the batcher flush path. The lock hold time correlates with a recent change in the batcher that groups micro-batches by tenant to improve throughput.
- When the lock holds, the connection's socket write-buffer fills and TCP backpressure pauses the read path; the frontend keeps the connection open but no more chunks are sent, which matches Velox's observation.
- In several traces we see sequence: create batch -> acquire lock -> heavy serde on a large token array -> hold lock -> flush -> release. The serde work is CPU-bound and happens while holding the lock.

Hypothesis: the tenant-grouping optimization improved throughput generally but amplifies tail latency in cases where a single tenant produces a very large output sequence. This leads to serialization stalls, per-connection write stalls, and client-observed open-but-silent sockets.

Attachments included: velox-prod-thread-dump-06014.txt, chunk-queue-metrics-20270614.csv

Short-term mitigations I can apply in a patch (estimated 25–35 minutes to roll):
- Change batcher config to use per-connection batching (disable tenant coalescing) — reduces batching efficiency but removes the lock contention surface.
- Move heavy serde off the critical lock (extract to per-batch worker after lock release) — small code change + quick rollback plan.
- Alternatively, apply routing to non-streaming endpoint (less invasive).

I'll prepare the quick patch and safety rollback; advise if we should route Velox off streaming while we apply.

-Marissa
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-06-15T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Production timeouts + partial chunks from Redwood streaming (Velox account) — exec update and action plan

Elena / Velox execs —

Executive update and immediate action plan (summary of steps we've taken & next 72h deliverables):

Immediate (completed):
- At 10:45 PT we applied a temporary routing policy that forces Velox traffic to our non-streaming endpoint. This removed the chunk serialization path and stopped new occurrences of the silent-open sockets within the first 6 minutes of the mitigation window. We monitored for 30 minutes: Velox 5xx dropped from 7.2% -> 0.21% and P95 latency for interactive calls returned to near-baseline.
- Rolled a hotfix branch that moves heavy serde out of the critical lock (rolled to canary nodes for Velox traffic only). Canary metrics show serialization tail reduced (340ms -> 14ms tail).

Near-term (next 24 hours):
- Complete rollout of the hotfix to all serving nodes for Velox traffic with automatic rollback on error signals.
- Run a controlled perf load to estimate throughput delta for non-streaming routing and publish expected QPS delta (will share by 17:00 PT today).

RCA & long-term (by 72 hours):
- Full RCA documenting the interaction between tenant coalescing and serde work; proposed permanent fix is to avoid holding locks during heavy CPU work and to add per-tenant size gates to batcher coalescing.
- Add alerting on "chunk_serialize_ms" tail and connection-silence detectors so we proactively detect regressions.

Attachments: proposed-fallback-policy-v1.docx (contains rollback runbook and routing policy).

I'll set up an exec sync at 16:00 PT today to walk through the rollout and answer questions. Sergio and Marissa remain owners for the technical rollout and RCA; I'll be the single point of contact to your CTO for executive status.

Apologies for the impact — we'll follow the timeline above and escalate if anything slips.

Jonas Weber
VP, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
